utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I said several times. This is another witness from the previous, and it was on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we show the top part of the statement or official record.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Do you see the name, very first line in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What was your question, Mr. Zec?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Deuric, after reading this statement, can you confirm that you were making lists of prisoners at Susica?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: You know that Predrag Bastah and Goran Viskovic were convicted before the Court of BiH for crimes committed at Vlasenica and Susica, do you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 24609.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: In front of you, Mr. Deuric, there will be the verdict of the Court of BiH against the accused Predrag Bastah and Goran Viskovic. This verdict was confirmed by the Appeals Chamber before the Court of BiH on 22nd February 2011. Veljko Basic was included in this trial and, due to his health, his case was separated. According to this verdict, Predrag Bastah was member of reserve police in Vlasenica and Goran Viskovic was member of the VRS. The court has found that the accused were guilty for a number of crimes including those committed in Susica in June and July 1992. They were found guilty for taking Susica prisoners away, many of whom are still missing. Goran Viskovic was also found guilty for taking prisoners away to perform forced labour and for the rape of one of the female prisoners. According to the verdict, the Susica guards were present while these crimes were taking place. Mr. Deuric, the reality is that the members of the VRS, police and guards committed numerous crimes against the Susica prisoners, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: It is so. But all sorts of stories went around. The rumour had it that --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Deuric, I'm referring what the judgement says. Can you confirm that? And you were there. You can confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this verdict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you asked a question, let's hear him out. Do you confirm, Mr. Deuric, that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I heard of murders, but I wasn't present. Let me tell you something else. People said that certain people were killed, and then a month later, I would see the person in question alive. People said that he or she tried to escape and was killed, and later on that person reappeared in the camp. Now, what sort of truth is that, and how should I believe it, because I could hear people talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I'm simply asking you what you saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only say what I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We don't have any objection to pages 1 through 12 of that document being admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6132, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Deuric, I would like to ask you about the conversation that you claim you had with Dragan Nikolic on the day of the funeral. You know that Dragan Nikolic pled guilty before this Tribunal for crimes committed at Susica. Do you know that? At --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: At his sentencing hearing, Witness Habiba Hadzic testified that she had lost her two sons at Susica, Enes and Bernes Hadzic. During her testimony she asked Dragan to tell her where her two sons were buried so at least she can find and bury them with dignity. This is at transcript page 247 of the Nikolic trial. Dragan Nikolic spoke shortly after her plea. He said that Enes and Bernes were taken from Susica on 30th September in a group of 40 other prisoners to Debelo Brdo. They were liquidated in that area so they could have been buried there. This is at transcript page 256 and 257. Mr. Deuric, the remaining prisoners of Susica were killed on 30th September 1992, after which the camp was closed. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: At the funeral when I was there on the 29th of September, two nephews and the son of two relatives were killed. Dragan Nikolic caught up with me when I was going home after the funeral. He says there's no one left at Susica. Everybody had been taken for an exchange. I did not answer anything, nor did I go back to Susica on the 26th of September. When that thing happened I went to the front line, and until the 29th, I did not even know that my nephews and relatives had been killed. And then I asked for a vehicle to go to the funeral, and I was late for the funeral. It was already underway. Now, what happened with those people who were left in Susica, I don't know. I did not ask him. I was in mourning. I wasn't thinking of anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: So I take it you didn't make any further inquiries after that. You didn't go to Susica. You went to Cerska?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: I went to Susica towards the end of 1994 from the front line, again to guard the TO building.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And this is in your statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have P40 -- P04856, e-court page 29. And at this page you will be able to see victims from Vlasenica, most of them Susica victims. In the middle of the page there are the names of Ms. Hadzic's sons. Enes was found in gravesite at Pelemis in 2004. Bernes is still missing. In this list there are names of other Susica prisoners, some of whom were found in a grave site at Ogradica in 2003. Do you know, Mr. Deuric, that Susica prisoners were buried at these locations after they were killed?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: No. No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know of any other location where Susica prisoners were buried?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: I can't say anything that I don't know. I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: That's fine. You told us that you had participated in the VRS combat operations at Cerska and Kravica in March 1993. You say that a group of Muslim fighters was stationed at mountain Udrc. You also --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Did you also -- did you also know that the Muslim civilians from the enclaves passed over this area on their way towards Tuzla? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: Yes. From Cerska they were on their way to Kladanj, as far as I know. And from Kladanj to Cerska and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And, in fact, the VRS units attacked and shelled these Muslim columns, civilians, who were passing over Udrc, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: Those who got out of Udrc, the Muslims, they attacked people from Krajina, and two people -- 12 people from Krajina were killed, and it is said that two Muslims were in that Krajina Brigade and that they got killed, too, and they were butchered, mutilated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: This is in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Can we have P04252, which is a combat report of 2nd March 1993, in which the command of the Zvornik Brigade informs the Drina Corps command that around 8 hours 30 minutes, columns of civilians and soldiers with pack animals were noticed from Udrc to -- and Rasevo towards Konjevic Polje. The columns were hit with every available weapon. This is in the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: The reality is, Mr. Deuric, that the VRS shelled and attacked the columns of civilian -- Muslim civilians, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: I did not understand. Which year was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: This is Udrc, Udrc mountain that you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: March 1993. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I was there in Cerska at the time when those men from the Krajina Brigade were killed. Now, what was going on over there, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And then you say you were fighting in Kravica, and your task at Kravica was to capture Kravica. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: When we crossed over there, there were no Muslims there. Kravica was held there until Christmas. We stayed there for seven or ten days in a place called Siljkovici, overlooking Kravica. That's when we found out that there's nothing left at Kravica. Everything was destroyed or had burned. We were looking for the church from the hilltop, looking to see if the church was destroyed too. And then we returned on the 21st of March because we got orders not to continue towards Srebrenica. We returned to Vlasenica and I was assigned to the Kladanj theatre, place called Cestane [phoen] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Zec, I wonder if you could conclude very soon. In terms of planning for the day, how much longer do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I will have one document to show the witness and I'll conclude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And while you were in Kravica, the VRS soldiers that you co-ordinated your activities, among them there was this battalion from the 1st Krajina Corps and there was special unit commanded by Mauzer. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: I think so. I know only for sure about the people from the Krajina Corps. As for Mauzer, some people said that there was also his unit there, but I was not anywhere in the vicinity. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: And can we have 65 ter 09320.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we're waiting, may I be of assistance with the transcript. On page 95, line 14, the witness did not say they were returning from Srebrenica from Kladanj, only to Cerska. And on page 96, line 18, and the witness said luckily -- or it's almost a miracle the church was not destroyed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We could not catch what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were just looking from a distance of a kilometre or two through the woods. We did not come close to see the church well enough, but all the other buildings had burnt down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Mr. Deuric, on the screen it's an order issued by the Drina Corps command pursuant to the military operation called Udar. Under 3 -- 2 -- 5.3, it provides that the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, a battalion of the 1st KK - if we can have 5.3, Mr. Registrar - and the 3rd Infantry Battalion were to attack along the villages of Banovici, Gornja Bacici and Kravica in order to crush the enemy and capture Kravica. Also to carry out operations in co-ordination with the special operations brigade commanded by Mauzer. You told us that Kravica was the area where you were deployed. This is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: You -- you were with the 3rd Infantry Battalion from Vlasenica fighting along with the soldiers from the 1st Krajina Corps. That's also what you already told us. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Commander Mauzer from this order is Ljubisa Savic, also known as Mauzer from Bijeljina. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We will receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6133, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZEC
utterances.text: I conclude my examination. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Deuric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you conclude in five minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure how this line 6 was interpreted to the witness. It says here you were in the 3rd Infantry Battalion from Vlasenica fighting along with the soldiers from the 1st Krajina Corps. Whereas the witness got interpretation that he was in the 1st Battalion, so I'm afraid confusion may arise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell us, Mr. Deuric, in which battalion, which unit were you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: I was in the Vlasenica battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was Mauzer in contact with your unit?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: No, he was not. I don't even know whether he was there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Whose settlement is Kravica? Who lives there, in the majority of almost 100 per cent?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: One hundred per cent Serbs, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At Udrc were there civilians based there? Which Muslims were at Udrc?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: A group came down from Udrc to the first village next door, Babici, and that's where the members of the 1st Krajina Corps were, and they killed them. And we got down along the whole length of Cerska. We didn't find anyone, no women, no children, no fighting men, no one. They were in hiding in the woods, and they committed this massacre in Udrc.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you say they captured and killed them there?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Captured was not recorded. So they took them captive, and then massacred them.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: Yes, including those two Muslims who were members of the Krajina Brigade. They butchered them, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just one more question. Wire was mentioned around the TO depot, barbed wire. When was it put up and for what reason?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: The barbed wire fence was put up on -- in 1976 when we came from Piskavica to Susica. We took it from the Elastik factory, and we took this used wire to make the fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Deuric. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR DEURIC
utterances.text: I would like to add something I forgot to say before. When Rogosija was attacked, it was a massacre. My elder nephew was unrecognisable, unidentifiable. He was burned, genitals were cut off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Deuric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This man Jankovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that's sufficient. We should stop here today, and that concludes your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On behalf of the Chamber, I thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you're free to go. We will rise all together and continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of February, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.48 p.m.,
